subject: Hyperburst: EOD latency spike — audit sample & retention questions
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa@finlytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:18:25 -0700
Subject: Urgent: production latency spike impacting EOD runs

Jordan —

We experienced a severe latency and error-rate spike in our EOD ingestion between 02:07–02:22 UTC this morning that caused ~18% of our batch jobs to time out and retry. Our ops team is asking for preserved runtime traces and the exact set of raw logs that correspond to those timestamps for a regulatory audit.

Specific asks:
- A preserved sample of request/response logs and runtime traces for 2027-09-14 02:00–02:30 UTC (we understand redaction may be required).
- Token-level cost/latency breakdown for those calls if available.
- Confirmation of retention policy and whether these records are on a legal hold.

We’re escalating to our security/compliance team and will likely request chain-of-custody evidence (hashes, manifests) if the regulator asks. Please advise what you can provide and the expected ETA.

Thanks —
Lisa Park
Head of Ops, Finlytics

---
Attachment: sla_escalation_notes.pdf (PDF stub, 75KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:42:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spike impacting EOD runs

Lisa —

Thanks for the heads up and the timestamps — really sorry for the disruption. We’re treating this as an exec-level escalation and will start preserving artifacts immediately. High-level plan:

1) Forensics preserve: we will snapshot request logs, KV/activation traces, and runtime latencies for the 02:00–02:30 UTC window and create a manifest with SHA256 hashes.
2) Sanitization: we’ll produce a redacted sample bundle (PII/PHI removed) suitable for your compliance review.
3) Chain-of-custody: we’ll include manifests, policy statements on retention, and an export audit log showing who accessed the bundle.

Can you confirm the regulator needs raw payloads or a redacted sample will suffice for now? Also looping in Marissa (CS) + Evelyn (Ops lead) to coordinate access and attestation. Expect an initial sample ETA in 6–8 hours, full bundle within 48 hours unless legal requires more.

-Jordan
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick action. A few exec-level asks before we send anything to Finlytics:

1) Scope & sample: Confirm the exact artifacts we will hand off in the initial sample and the sanitization rules (list fields that will be redacted).
2) Evidence of preservation: include the manifest with SHA256, the snapshot command logs (who ran them, timestamp), and our internal retention policy snippet.
3) Chain-of-custody attestation: legal/security wants a short statement signed by our security lead confirming the bundle wasn’t modified post-snapshot. Coordinate with Security to issue that.
4) Exec note: prepare a one-page summary for Finlytics execs describing what happened, the mitigations in flight, and the timeline for a full root-cause.

I’m scheduling a 30-minute sync at 17:00 PDT (link below) to approve the bundle before we share. Please have the sample link and manifest uploaded before the call. If Security can’t provide the attestation in time, include a stub noting ’attestation pending’ and timeline.
